lede: We rebuilt the lost program from the paper, put the 2009 yeast data back together and reran every experiment. {attempted} of {items} results were attempted: {exact} exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly, {inconclusive} inconclusive, {differs} differ. The method runs; its curves do not come back.
items_caption: Every figure, table and number in the paper, with the verdict check_results.py computes from our run.
claims_line: Main claim, SSL beats SVM and reaches sensitivity 0.92 at 1 minus specificity 0.09: differs and differs on our run (SVM leads at every training size; best SSL sensitivity at 0.09 is 0.20). Weighted beats binary: agrees. Two Discussion claims fail in the paper's own Table 1 (paper errors); the rest differ for a cause still open.
came_back: The Tong 2004 screen, BioGRID interactions and Gavin and Ho complexes from SGD's copy of 2009-12-19; 48129 complex edges against about 49,000; 4747 deletion-array genes against about 4,700.
Divisive correlation clustering, eq. 2 weights, the 10 properties and 18 features, label spreading and an RBF SVM, as the package fgnssl.
SSL area under the ROC curve 0.664 on the weighted network, 0.656 on the binary one, as the paper orders them.
SGI pairs have the higher average degree and closeness, as the Discussion says.
buried: The ROC curves. SSL reaches 0.675 to 0.645 under the curve and SVM 0.705 to 0.678; the paper's curves enclose about 0.95.
SSL over SVM. SVM leads at every training size on our run.
Table 1 and Fig. 6. Our KS statistics differ; the paper's P-values imply about 5,531 pairs per test, ours 3,029.
Eisen's 1998 heat-shock time course; the paper's protein-interaction filter, SSL settings, SVM grid and seeds.
matched_intro: What we fixed to make the run, and where it came from.
matched: Two-hybrid and Affinity Capture-Western, 13007 interactions (paper 12,990), the closest interpretable filter.
Tong query genes by the non-essential deletion array, 586472 tested pairs.
alpha 0.99, sigma chosen on the training labels.
RBF kernel, C and gamma by grid search on the training folds.
closing: We dug up You et al. 2010 on 13 November 2026. The method came back as a package; its results did not.
